name: stability
description: Institutional and political stability: how predictable and durable the government and institutions are (government crises, early elections, coups, institutional conflicts). 0 = state collapse or no functioning government, 50 = recurring government crises, 100 = fully stable and predictable institutions. Violence and terrorism are NOT included (see 'violence risk').

name: corruption
description: Corruption in public institutions: 0 = practically none, 50 = widespread petty and political corruption, 100 = state captured by corrupt networks.

name: happiness
description: Average life satisfaction: from 2005 about 10 x the Gallup/World Happiness Report Cantril ladder (0-10), corrected only with a reason; before 2005 an estimate on the same scale (0 = mass despair, 100 = very high satisfaction).

name: social revanchism
description: Revanchism of SOCIETY: strength of popular wish to regain lost territory, influence or great-power status: 0 = none, 50 = widespread among the public, 100 = dominant public mood.

name: war exhaustion
description: Weariness of the population with war, also after a past war and without an ongoing one: 0 = none, 50 = clear opposition to further war effort, 100 = refusal to keep fighting.

name: government popularity
description: Approval of the government / leader: percent approving in opinion polls where reliable polls exist; elsewhere an estimate on the same 0-100 scale (0 = universally rejected, 100 = near-universal support).

name: social sensitivity
description: Sensitivity to costs: how quickly losses (casualties, falling incomes, rising prices) turn into opposition to the government and its policy. 0 = society bears large losses without reaction, 100 = small losses cause strong opposition.

name: civilization level
description: Development of the society on an absolute scale (education, technology, health, institutions, quality of life), seeded as 100 x HDI: ~30 = least developed countries today, ~95 = most developed today; rises when a country develops even if others do too.

name: assimilation
description: How well immigrants and minorities integrate into the majority society: 0 = isolated parallel societies, 100 = full assimilation.

name: immigration crisis
description: 1 = a serious immigration crisis at any time during the year (mass, poorly controlled inflow causing a national political or social crisis).

name: riots
description: 1 = serious riots at any time during the year (large-scale, violent, nationally significant unrest; peaceful protests and isolated incidents do not count).

name: epidemic
description: 1 = a serious epidemic at any time during the year (significant mortality or disruption of normal life, e.g. COVID-19 in 2020-2021).

name: mobilized
description: 1 = partial or full military mobilisation at any time during the year; possible without an ongoing war.

name: net migration
description: Net migration intensity (immigrants minus emigrants per year, relative to population): seeded as 5 x net migration per 1000 inhabitants, so +-20 per mille = +-100; negative = net emigration.

name: state collapse
description: 1 = the state collapsed at any time during the year: central government lost control over most of the territory or ceased to function (e.g. Somalia 1991, Libya 2011, Yemen 2015); affects the country and its neighbours.

name: government revanchism
description: Revanchism of the GOVERNMENT: how much official policy aims to regain lost territory, influence or great-power status: 0 = none, 50 = a recurring policy goal, 100 = central goal of state policy (e.g. Russia after 2008 ~80).

name: violence risk
description: Risk of politically motivated violence and terrorism (unrest, insurgency, terror attacks, armed conflict on the territory): 0 = practically none, 50 = recurring violent incidents, 100 = constant large-scale violence. Seeded as 50 - 20 x WGI Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism.
